subject: Verdant Tech integration: smoke + load scenario review and validation
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@verdanttech.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Verdant tech – initial smoke + load scenarios for Redwood runtime

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the time last week. Verdant’s integration engineer team put together a short set of smoke and load scenarios focused on three areas we flagged in the architecture review: (1) model variant fallback across dedicated pools, (2) prefix/KV cache behavior for chat sessions, and (3) sustained token throughput under batching at 8k context.

I attached a condensed test plan (verdant_test_plan_v1.xlsx) and an updated network diagram (network_diagram_v2.png). High level asks from us:
- Can Redwood run the three scenarios in your Staging-Dedicated cluster next week?
- We’d like results logged in the PoC results format you shared (see attachment sample poc_results_20261210.log).
- Which internal owners at Redwood should we coordinate scheduling and access with?

We can be flexible on windows — prefer Wed/Thu next week for the load window.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Integration Lead, Verdant Tech
T: +1 415 555 0198

Attachments: verdant_test_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), network_diagram_v2.png (image)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@verdanttech.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Verdant tech – initial smoke + load scenarios for Redwood runtime

Hi Tom — thanks for the artifacts. I’ve skimmed the plan and it looks like you captured the right vectors. Quick answers:
- Yes — we can reserve a staging Dedicated pool for a controlled load window.
- We’ll ingest your PoC log format; Marcus will map the fields to our telemetry pipeline.
- Owners: Sergio will be lead for execution & scheduling; Marcus will handle telemetry/metrics; I’ll own acceptance criteria and the final architecture sign-off.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sergio to propose 2x windows (Wed/Thu) and a duration (2–4 hours).
2) Verdant to confirm test accounts and any JWT/KMS access required.
3) Marcus to share the mapping doc and a dashboard template we’ll use for pass/fail.

Can you confirm if the test uses streaming responses for the large-context scenario? If so we’ll ensure the streaming gateway is included in the run.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Partner Engineering — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Laura / Marcus — I’ll take lead on scheduling and execution. Notes from my read:
- We should run the model-variant fallback test at lower concurrency first to validate deterministic fallback behavior, then ramp.
- For KV/prefix cache: we need to ensure Verdant’s session tokens map to our cache keys; ask them to include a stable session_id in payloads.
- For the 8k batching run, I want to run two variants: 32B float16 quantized (cost light) and a 70B int8 surrogate. That will give Verdant numbers for cost/latency tradeoffs.

I’ll propose windows: 2026-12-22 09:00–12:00 PT and 2026-12-23 13:00–16:00 PT. Marcus — can you prepare the dashboard template and the telemetry mapping by EOD Monday?

Sergio
